After lunch, responsibilities for gate calls
The aim of this section is to explain the main rule first, then the reasons

Companion Animal Travel Desk Service Standards

This section sets the standard for careful, respectful handling of pet travel requests and service changes. The Companion Animal Travel Desk supports travelers and their animals by keeping arrangements clear, accurate, and humane.

Staff must greet each traveler in a warm professional tone and treat each journey as a shared responsibility. When a customer arrives with a concern, the desk should listen fully, confirm the travel need, and record the service change in the desk ledger before any action is taken. <<FACT F068>> The desk must never promise a service that cannot be completed within the approved travel terms, and any exception must be handled only through the proper review path.

When confirming arrangements, staff should use plain language and avoid confusion. If a crate, carrier, or related item is presented, the condition of the item must be checked against the accepted travel standard, and any concern must be raised immediately. A traveler should receive clear guidance on what has been accepted, what requires correction, and what follow-up is needed before departure. The desk should remain courteous even when a request cannot be approved, because calm and consistent communication protects the animal, the traveler, and the service.

All notes must be complete, readable, and entered without delay so that other staff can rely on the record. If the service plan changes, the updated instruction must be reflected in the ledger and relayed to the next responsible station. The desk must also preserve privacy and avoid discussing a traveler’s arrangements with anyone who is not assigned to the case.

If the desk encounters any uncertainty, staff must stop and seek guidance rather than guess. Contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor for any unresolved matter, and continue only when the next instruction is received.
